samples.summary: Deleting the mirror also deleted the only tests guarding this repo's `.github/workflows/agent-*.yml` invariants; those workflows all stay here and are now unguarded.
samples.evidence: The comment here asserts the deleted suites "moved to wafflebase/agent-pipeline, where that repo's own CI runs them". That is true for tests of pipeline CODE, but several deleted tests asserted properties of THIS repo's workflow YAML, which is not part of the vendored pipeline: `glob .github/workflows/agent-*.yml` still returns all ten files, and the diff itself edits `agent-implement.yml` and `ci.yml`. Concretely lost, with no replacement anywhere in `scripts/`: `checks.test.mjs`'s "every workflow that runs a pipeline script sets GH_REPO", "agent-fix decides eligibility on TRUSTED main, before the branch checkout", "agent-fix re-verifies the commit AFTER checkout", and "the panel starts with CI... concurrency group must agree with the gate"; `rounds.test.mjs`'s "the gate job's literal copy of the latch matches the module" (agent-review-panel.yml); `loop-status.test.mjs`'s "DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS matches the panel workflow's env literal", "the CI attempts guard's literal latch predicate matches the module's rule" (agent-iterate-ci.yml) and "REGRESSION: a fixer cancelled during setup must not consume a round" (which pinned that the two DISPATCH_FILE declarations agree and that nothing sits between recording the round and the fixer); `fix-report.test.mjs`'s "the fixer prompt orders the report BEFORE the push"; `panel-round-comment.test.mjs`'s "the panel workflow actually posts the round comment"; `review-panel.test.mjs`'s upload-artifact `include-hidden-files` and capture-meta wiring assertions. I grepped every remaining `scripts/**/*.test.mjs` for `workflows` — the only hits are `ci-workflow.test.mjs`/`changed-areas.test.mjs` (CI lanes, not agent workflows) and `harvest.test.mjs:313`, which uses `.github/workflows/ci.yml` merely as a fixture string. Even if the pipeline repo now hosts those tests, they would read ITS `.github/workflows`, not this repo's, so these workflow files can drift freely from here on.

samples.summary: `readPins` is exported "for the test file" but has zero tests, and it silently drops tag-pinned checkouts — the invariant the deleted `checks.test.mjs` guarded — while the job it gates is now blocking.
samples.evidence: `readPins` only records a ref matching `/^\s*ref:\s*([0-9a-f]{40})\b/`; a non-SHA ref is skipped, not reported. So if one of the 18 `repository: wafflebase/agent-pipeline` blocks were changed to `ref: v1.2.0`, `pins.size` would still be 1 and `main()` would print success. The deleted `checks.test.mjs` had exactly this test ("every agent-pipeline checkout pins an immutable commit SHA, not a tag"), collecting `offenders` per checkout — that is gone. `scripts/test/verify-pipeline-drift.test.mjs` imports only `mirrorImports` and `reappearedMirrorFiles` (line 27); `grep readPins` across the repo returns only its definition (:95) and its single call site (:178). The split-pin branch at :180-187 is likewise unexercised. This matters more now, not less: the diff makes `pipeline-drift` blocking (ci.yml), so the job reads as coverage of pin integrity that it does not actually provide.

samples.summary: Three behaviour changes to the vendored-copy integrity checker (`walkVendor` recursion, broadened `assertClosed` matcher + resolved-path targets, non-code ASSETS) ship with no test file for this script at all.
samples.evidence: `glob scripts/test/*.mjs` returns six test files and none is `vendor-pipeline.test.mjs`; `grep vendor-pipeline` finds no test importing it. Yet this diff adds: (1) `walkVendor` at :66, a new recursive walk that replaces the previous flat `readdirSync(VENDOR).filter(f => f.endsWith('.mjs'))` and now drives the "unlisted file present" check at :180 — if it regressed to non-recursive, an extra file dropped into `vendor/pipeline/lenses/` would go unreported and the only tamper-detection for the vendored tree would be silently narrower; (2) the `assertClosed` regex at :97, broadened to side-effect imports and single quotes — the docblock at :87-90 says the old one "would have passed [an unclosed side-effect import] and failed at runtime instead", i.e. a fixed bug with no regression test; (3) the target resolution at :103, whose own comment concedes "No nested module is vendored today, so this is latent" — an admittedly unexercised code path. None of these is exported, so no test could reach them without a refactor. The sibling `scripts/test/verify-pipeline-drift.test.mjs` shows the tmpdir-tree pattern that would cover them.

samples.summary: New `pipelineDir()` resolution and the `review` skip path are added to a module that already has a test file, with no test for any of their three branches.
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.test.mjs` (read in full, 73 lines) covers `isValidSlug`, `parseRepoFromRemoteUrl`, `renderPrBody`, `commitsMissingTrailer` and the disclosure predicates — nothing touches the new code. `pipelineDir` at :139-149 has three distinct outcomes: (a) no `--pipeline-dir` and no `AGENT_PIPELINE_DIR` → `null`, which drives the new warn-and-return skip at :336-343; (b) a directory containing `packages/pipeline/review-panel.mjs` → returns the inner path, which is then used for BOTH `--lenses-dir` and the panel script; (c) anything else → `fail()`. The env-var fallback at :140 is untested, and branch (c) fires for a path that does not exist at all while the message asserts "is not a checkout of wafflebase/agent-pipeline" — a mis-diagnosis no test would catch. `pipelineDir` is not exported, so it is currently unreachable from the test file.

samples.summary: `reappearedMirrorFiles` is only tested with root-level files, so a nested pipeline-owned path reappearing — the exact shape this diff creates by moving `scripts/agent/lenses/` away — is uncovered.
samples.evidence: All four new cases pass single-segment or STAYS-excluded paths: `{"severity.mjs": ""}` (:152), `{"vendor/pipeline/severity.mjs"}` (:163), measurement files (:168), `package.json` (:177). This diff renames `scripts/agent/lenses/*.md` and `lenses.json` into `vendor/pipeline/lenses/`, making `lenses/` a pipeline-owned directory that is NOT in `STAYS` — so `scripts/agent/lenses/correctness.md` reappearing is a live regression path with no test. The `.sort()` at verify-pipeline-drift.mjs:126 is also unexercised, since no case returns more than one file; the multi-file ordering the error message depends on is unasserted.

samples.summary: `set-state.mjs` and `session-job-summary.mjs` are still executed from this repo's tree, but their test files were deleted here and nothing local covers their behaviour.
samples.evidence: agent-implement.yml:285 and :362 invoke `./scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/set-state.mjs` and `.../session-job-summary.mjs` directly from this repo's checkout (the `implement` job has no pipeline adapter — vendor-pipeline.mjs:38-43 says exactly this). The diff deletes `scripts/agent/set-state.test.mjs` and `scripts/agent/session-job-summary.test.mjs` and vendors only the modules, not their tests. `scripts/vendor-pipeline.mjs` verifies sha256 bytes against `VENDOR.json`, which proves the file is unmodified but says nothing about whether the pinned upstream commit's own suite passed. The same applies to the other 18 vendored modules that the retained measurement half imports (`severity.mjs`, `review-panel.mjs`, `rounds.mjs`, `metrics.mjs`, `novelty.mjs`...), whose local suites are all deleted here. This may be an intentional division of responsibility, but no check in this repo enforces the upstream half of it.

verdict.reason: No test in the working tree exercises `readPins` or the SHA-not-tag pin invariant. `scripts/verify-pipeline-drift.mjs:95-107` builds pins only from refs matching `/^\s*ref:\s*([0-9a-f]{40})\b/`, so a tag-pinned checkout is silently skipped rather than reported, and `main()` at :178-188/:234-236 still succeeds. The sole test file, `scripts/test/verify-pipeline-drift.test.mjs:27`, imports only `mirrorImports` and `reappearedMirrorFiles`; all 19 of its tests route through `check()`/`reappeared()` (:40-48, :141-149), leaving `readPins`, the `pins.size === 0` branch, and the split-pin branch (:179-187) entirely unexercised. I searched wide for a counterexample: all six files in `scripts/test/` (`ci-workflow.test.mjs` asserts only matrix/RUN_HEAVY job structure), repo-wide greps for `[0-9a-f]{40}`, `immutable commit`, `SHA-pinned`, `SHA_REF`, `workflowDir`, and `wafflebase/agent-pipeline` restricted to test files, plus `.github/` for an actionlint/zizmor/dependabot policy (none exists). The only test asserting "every agent-pipeline checkout pins an immutable commit SHA, not a tag" is `.trusted/scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:293,329-344`, and `.trusted/` is a snapshot of the deleted mirror (it contains only `scripts/agent/**` plus node_modules; `scripts/verify-pipeline-drift.mjs` is absent there) that no lane runs. The reviewer was factually wrong about one detail — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:325-326` does contain `grep -oE 'ref: [0-9a-f]{40}'` — but that inline shell step is not a test and only re-implements the split-pin count with the same tag-skipping flaw (`COUNT` stays 1 when a ref is a tag), so it is not a counterexample. The gated job is now blocking (ci.yml:301-352) across 19 `repository: wafflebase/agent-pipeline` blocks, so this is a changed behavior with no meaningful test: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

I also chased the indirect routes: the only subprocess-invoking test (verify-self-lanes.test.mjs:28) runs verify-self.mjs, not this script; and the tested twin scripts/verify-pipeline-drift.mjs exports walk/mirrorImports/readPins behind an import.meta.url guard (:242) so its test can import them, whereas vendor-pipeline.mjs exports nothing and has no such guard, so no existing test can reach its internals. The closest live exercise is ci.yml:344 running the verifier against the real passing tree, which would still exit 0 if walkVendor regressed to flat or the matcher narrowed — a smoke invocation, not regression coverage. Major by impact: the unlisted-file check is the only tamper detection for the vendored tree.
